input.title: One Sheet
input.sourceText:
EXT. OCEAN - DAWN

The same paper boat floats alone in the blue water. Its folded paper stretches into canvas; its bow curves into polished timber. The tiny vessel grows into a full-size mahogany sailing yacht. The sea opens around it.

story.about: A paper boat on a desk, caught between stillness and impermanence, becomes a metaphor for a forgotten dream or a moment suspended in time
story.whyCare: The viewer cares because the image evokes loss, beauty, and the quiet weight of memory — universal emotions tied to objects that hold meaning
story.hook: A paper boat rests on a dark timber desk — fragile, alone, yet charged with unseen history
story.beginning: The scene opens with a still life: a paper boat, a crease, a bead of water — all elements frozen in a moment of quiet tension
story.development: The camera lingers on the details — the light catching the crease, the water touching the bow — suggesting something about to be revealed or already lost
story.tension: The stillness implies a past event or an impending change — the water may be a tear, a memory, or a sign of decay
story.payoff: The image remains unresolved — the boat stays untouched, the water still, the light unchanged — leaving the audience to wonder what was lost and whether it can be reclaimed
story.ending: The scene ends without action, reinforcing the theme of silence and the permanence of absence
story.withheld: The identity of the owner, the reason for the boat’s presence, and the nature of the water are never revealed — keeping the mystery intact
amplify: Emphasize the contrast between the darkness of the desk and the thin line of light

Use shallow depth of field to isolate the paper boat from the surrounding workshop
